gates.result: BLOCKED - ENVIRONMENT, NOT THE FIX: the AVD's Chromium web-content a11y bridge (org.chromium.webview_shell 124.0.6367.219) stopped exposing the WebView subtree to the INSTALLED accessibility service (every loop observation = 'unusable tree (6 lines, pageNodes=2)'), so the loop never reached 3 guard-pass refusals during the smoke window. This is the documented Phase-6/6.3 AVD disease (phase-6-status.json blocker: 'intermittent all day ... never held this afternoon'), reproduced today across: pocketpet-test warm snapshot boot, cold -no-snapshot boot, windowed AND headless, pm clear org.chromium.webview_shell (with the service verified bound first), touch-exploration toggle (inert: no service requests the capability), UiAutomation dump-pulsing, and a brand-new AVD (pocketpet-cardfix, same system image). The bridge DID engage for ~2 minutes today at 10:43-10:45 (see 'observed_once'), which is how the interactive card was reached and observed on screen once.

observed_once.what: During the 10:42-10:45 window the bridge engaged and a full autoDeny=false stub run reached the interactive completion card on-device (fixed build installed since 09:41).

logcat 10-07 10:45:03.505: 'exit: 3 consecutive guard-pass refusals - completion card (max one per task, vision 04 section 3 Path C)' - the Path-C trigger in the real loop, autoDeny=false

owner_device_equivalence_note: On this emulator image SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW appops 'default' resolves as overlay-ALLOWED (manifest permission granted at install; MODE_DEFAULT defers to it) - verified live: the 10:44:04 card took the overlay path with appops still 'default'. The owner's S25+ shows the same appops 'default' yet the card was INVISIBLE - device-specific appops/permission resolution. The fix's bring-to-front branch is keyed on Settings.canDrawOverlays(), so the smoke forced the owner's state explicitly with 'appops set navigator.app SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW deny' (verified 'deny') - every batch after 10:53 ran with the deny in force, so any card would have exercised the bring-to-front path.
